channel.title: The Coin Wire
channel.description: Crypto news on Bitcoin, Ethereum, DeFi, stablecoins, exchanges, regulation and protocol upgrades: what changed, and what comes next.

item.title: Why a rebasing token’s pool balance can look wrong
item.description: A rebasing token can change a pool’s live balance without a trade, while an AMM’s stored reserves lag; compare both before reading price or liquidity.

item.title: Five Steps to Fund a Polygon Wallet Before Minting
item.description: A Polygon collectible mint needs the right network, payment token and gas balance; these five checks help you choose a funding route and avoid a failed transaction.

item.title: Multi-Hop Swaps: How to Read the Route Before You Trade
item.description: A multi-hop swap routes one token through intermediate assets; compare its net output, fees, price impact and minimum received with a direct route before signing.

item.title: Blast will wind down as operating costs outrun revenue
item.description: Blast will wind down after saying network costs exceed revenue, while users face a weeklong withdrawal pause and an Oct. 26 deadline for its standard withdrawal interface.

item.title: Solana Swap Slippage: Set a Limit, Not a Price Target
item.description: Slippage tolerance sets the worst output a Solana swap will accept; learn how it differs from price impact, how to size it and when a failed trade is the better result.

item.title: How Much ETH Should a Treasury Keep for Token Swaps?
item.description: A treasury’s ETH reserve should cover measured swap and approval gas under stressed conditions, with a separate buffer for timing, chain choice and operational delays.

item.title: Bridge the right assets before joining a Polygon pool
item.description: Before joining a Polygon pool, move the exact supported token to Polygon PoS, keep POL for gas, and confirm the pool’s network and token contract.

item.title: Why Avalanche Pool Prices Can Mislead Smart Contracts
item.description: A pool’s spot price describes its current balance, not a reliable market value; thin liquidity, trade size and oracle design can change what a contract should trust.

item.title: A token swap estimate is a quote, not a promise
item.description: A token swap estimate combines pool price, fees, route depth and slippage; checking those parts before signing shows what can change before on-chain settlement.

item.title: Reading a BNB Chain Wallet’s Token History
item.description: Search your wallet address in a block explorer, then read token transfers alongside the transactions that caused them to distinguish payments, swaps and approvals.

item.title: SEC proposes conditional self-custody for crypto funds
item.description: The SEC proposed allowing advisers and regulated funds to self-custody some crypto, with board oversight, key controls and annual accountant reports as checks.

item.title: A Token Pause Can Stall One Leg of a Polygon Bridge Transfer
item.description: A token pause can block one leg of a Polygon Bridge transfer without stopping the bridge itself; check the transaction state before retrying or seeking recovery.

item.title: Utexo plans to bring USDT back to Bitcoin through RGB
item.description: Tether-backed Utexo plans to issue USDT on Bitcoin via RGB this month, reviving the token’s original network while testing a more private payment model.

item.title: Why a Wrapped Bridge Token May Not Redeem Yet
item.description: A wrapped bridge token is redeemable only through the route and contract that issued it; delays, liquidity gaps and paused bridges explain many failures.

item.title: A Swap Is Not Complete When the First Chain Says Success
item.description: Tracking an omnichain swap links source confirmation to destination execution, showing route progress and why one transaction hash alone cannot prove delivery.

item.title: BaseSwap on Base: swaps and liquidity carry different risks
item.description: BaseSwap lets Base users swap tokens or supply liquidity; the choice turns on convenience versus pool risk, and on what providers need to track after depositing.

item.title: SEC proposes conditional crypto self-custody for advisers and funds
item.description: SEC proposal would let advisers and funds self-custody some crypto when no qualified custodian is available, with controls and board oversight.

item.title: Is Chainflip Right for Your Cross-Chain Swap?
item.description: Chainflip swaps native assets across chains without wrapped tokens, but the right route depends on custody, asset availability and how much coordination a swap requires.

item.title: FCA opens crypto authorisation gateway ahead of 2027 rules
item.description: The FCA opened crypto authorisation on 30 September, giving firms until February to seek approval before broader rules take effect in October 2027.
